newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister says "disinformation" over Zaire.
newsitem.headline: French minister says "disinformation" over Zaire.

text.p: A French minister said on Wednesday that the world suffered "disinformation" in scant media coverage on the plight of Rwandan refugees in Zaire.
Xavier Emmanuelli, junior Minister for Emergency Humanitarian Action, said there was a "strange manipulation" of the media but refused to say whom he considered responsible.

France championed calls to send a U.N. force to Zaire to protect an estimated 1.2 million refugees trapped by fighting between Rwandan-backed rebels and the Zairean army. The plan was scrapped when most refugees returned home late last year.
"These efforts got lost in the sand. There has really been disinformation," Emmanuelli told a New Year reception.
"It was claimed that everyone had gone home. Three quarters of them have gone home, it's true. That implicitly means that 250,000 people are sacrificed."

Many other nations were reluctant to commit troops to Zaire, some of them suspecting France of a wider hidden agenda in wanting to prop up the government of the sprawling French-speaking country facing rebel advances in the east.
Emmanuelli's office said later that overflights by the charity Aviation without Borders estimated that 350,000 refugees were still in the regions of Kisangani and Shabunda in eastern Zaire.

It said the French ministry had had representatives in Kisangani since last November and had sent in aid worth 15 million francs ($3 million). Two French planes were due to fly food for children into Kisangani from Nairobi this week.
Two relief groups said on Tuesday that the lack of food and water was pushing up the death toll among Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire and urged the world to do more to help them.

Paris-based Medecins sans Frontieres (Doctors without Borders) and the U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF) said more than 20 people a day were dying, up from 10 a day in late December, at the Tingi Tingi camp, which has 120,000 refugees.
